blocks.heading: Responding to community needs
blocks.text: A community includes customers, workers, nearby residents and other organisations. Businesses can respond by supplying needed goods and services, creating work, purchasing from local suppliers and supporting useful local projects. A response is stronger when the business first identifies a specific need rather than assuming that everyone wants the same thing. Community benefit and business benefit may coincide, but a useful service can still be costly to provide.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Families near Omuti Foods need bread before the early bus leaves, and the bakery has an unused early shift. Opening earlier could make breakfast purchases more convenient and increase sales if enough families use the service. Hiring local workers can bring household income into the area. The bakery must compare the extra demand with wages, electricity and transport costs: a community response is more sustainable when it can be maintained without exhausting the business’s resources.
